memory_candidates.content: When building a verify-deploy.sh (or similar) fixture test that copies agent-system/extensions/ into a scratch dir to exercise real deploy-tree gates, use a REAL rsync copy (excluding large vendored dirs like a Python venv) rather than symlinks. Several deploy-time lints use `find ... -type f` / `-type d` without `-L`, which does NOT follow symlinked directories or files -- a symlink-only fixture produces spurious 'no dispatchable agents found' / 'no manifests found' failures unrelated to the thing actually under test. A full real copy of agent-system/extensions/ (minus vendored deps) is typically small (~16 MB for this repo) and fast (a few seconds) once the one large offender is excluded.

orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's live preflight write path (skill_preflight_update -> update-task-status.sh) leaks an unredirected `echo "OK: task N status -> X"` onto cycle-plan.sh's own stdout, ahead of the final JSON line. This does not break the lead in production because the lead is an LLM reading Bash tool output loosely, not performing a literal `jq` parse -- but any literal jq-based consumer of orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's stdout (including a test fixture) must extract the trailing JSON line specifically (e.g. `grep '^{' | tail -n1`) rather than parsing the raw captured stdout directly.

Severity-gate config pattern for verify-deploy.sh-style gates: a small source-store JSON config (ceiling/baseline values + derivation notes) paired with one env-var mode toggle (default warn, promotable to hard in a deliberate follow-up commit -- never a persisted 'N stable deploys' auto-promotion counter) and normalized (value-free) warn()/fail() finding text. This repo now has two independent instances (claudemd-size-budget.json/SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE_GATE_MODE and orchestrator-context-budget.json/ORCHESTRATOR_BUDGET_GATE_MODE); a short context/patterns/ note documenting the shared shape would help a third instance land correctly on the first try.
